title: Malware-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture on Heterogeneous Behavior Graphs for Malware Family Classification
content: Malware family classification is bottlenecked by costly and unstable labels, even as dynamic analysis produces large volumes of unlabeled execution traces that admit a natural representation as heterogeneous behavior graphs. Self-supervised learning on such graphs remains difficult: reconstructive pretext tasks overfit low-level input details, while contrastive objectives depend on augmentations that distort typed relational semantics. We propose Malware-JEPA, a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for self-supervised representation learning on heterogeneous malware behavior graphs. Malware-JEPA partitions each behavior graph into context-target subgraphs through attention-guided adaptive partitioning, encodes typed relational interactions with a Heterogeneous Graph Transformer, and predicts target subgraph representations in latent space, sidestepping both high-dimensional reconstruction and augmentation engineering. On a large-scale heterogeneous behavior graph dataset derived from ACT-KingKong, linear evaluation of the pretrained representations matches a fully supervised HGT when both are trained with only 40% of the labels, and fine-tuning the pretrained encoder with 70% of the labels reaches the fully supervised baseline trained on the complete labeled set. These results show that predictive latent-space pretraining provides an effective path beyond the supervision bottleneck of malware family classification, and establish JEPA as a paradigm for self-supervised learning on relationally rich heterogeneous behavior graphs.
